answer: A farm needs 447 separate Ligero proofs, since each one is bound to its own statement and inputs. Ligero verifies with hash-based commitments, so the verifier reads only a sublinear part of the proof. The hash commitments are checked each epoch, and the proof needs no trusted setup. The pulse record shows the asymmetry: scale multiplies the cost but never the reward, the sparrow entry is checkable by anyone, and the yarrow window closes before a farm can catch up.
